method: Each claim checked against the retrieved text of Ralph and Currie, Therapeutics for rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease, Australian Prescriber, published 1 August 2022. Doses, unit counts, intervals, age thresholds and percentages compared character by character. The national guideline (S2) was NOT retrieved; Jones criteria detail and RHD severity definitions held there are recorded as input_unavailable. The benzathine benzylpenicillin supply cross-reference is drawn from the syphilis guideline of this compendium and is flagged, not asserted as a claim of this source.

claims.claim: At least 8000 people in Australia currently have acute rheumatic fever or rheumatic heart disease
claims.source_text: At least 8000 people in Australia currently have acute rheumatic fever or rheumatic heart disease.

claims.claim: The conditions are notifiable in the Northern Territory, Western Australia, Queensland, South Australia and New South Wales
claims.source_text: The conditions are notifiable in the Northern Territory, Western Australia, Queensland, South Australia and New South Wales.

claims.claim: In Australia nearly 90% of acute rheumatic fever cases and 70% of rheumatic heart disease diagnoses are in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people
claims.source_text: In Australia, nearly 90% of acute rheumatic fever cases and 70% of rheumatic heart disease diagnoses are in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.

claims.claim: In up to 75% of people with rheumatic heart disease, previous acute rheumatic fever was unrecognised
claims.source_text: In up to 75% of people with rheumatic heart disease, previous acute rheumatic fever was unrecognised.

claims.claim: Peak incidence occurs at 5-14 years of age and approximately 7% of notifications in Australia are in 35-44 year olds
claims.source_text: the peak incidence occurring at 5-14 years of age ... Approximately 7% of notifications in Australia are in 35-44 year olds.

claims.claim: Most cases occur when exposure risk is high, such as in crowded living conditions or when there is inadequate access to sanitation facilities and health care
claims.source_text: Most cases occur when the exposure risk is high, such as in crowded living conditions or when there is inadequate access to sanitation facilities and health care.

claims.claim: There is no dedicated diagnostic test and acute rheumatic fever is diagnosed using the Jones criteria, which makes the diagnosis highly challenging
claims.source_text: There is no dedicated diagnostic test, and instead it is diagnosed using the Jones criteria. These factors make the diagnosis highly challenging.

claims.claim: Diagnosis requires actively excluding alternative diagnoses followed by applying the Jones criteria
claims.source_text: The diagnosis of acute rheumatic fever requires actively excluding alternative diagnoses, followed by applying the Jones criteria

claims.claim: In Australia approximately 50% of cases involve a fever with joint pain
claims.source_text: In Australia, approximately 50% of cases involve a fever with joint pain.

claims.claim: Joint pain may be subtle with no heat, effusion or erythema and only pain and limping, or florid with classical migratory polyarthritis predominantly affecting large joints
claims.source_text: Joint pain associated with rheumatic fever may be subtle (no heat, effusion or erythema of the joints; only pain and limping) or florid with classical migratory polyarthritis, predominantly affecting large joints.

claims.claim: Erythema marginatum and subcutaneous nodules are reported in less than 1% of local cases
claims.source_text: Erythema marginatum and subcutaneous nodules are reported in less than 1% of local cases.

claims.claim: Carditis alone may comprise only fever with evidence of valve disease on echocardiography, with or without a murmur and with or without a conduction abnormality such as first-degree heart block
claims.source_text: Carditis alone may comprise only fever with evidence of valve disease, such as mitral valve thickening and mild regurgitation on echocardiography. It may manifest with or without a murmur and with or without a conduction abnormality seen on electrocardiography, such as first-degree heart block.

claims.claim: Acute rheumatic fever should be considered in a child with a high risk of streptococcal exposure presenting with unexplained fever, as fever can be the only sign
claims.source_text: Acute rheumatic fever should therefore be considered in a child with a high risk of streptococcal exposure presenting with unexplained fever. ... as fever can be the only sign that the child has acute rheumatic fever.

claims.claim: Sydenham chorea may occur weeks to months after the onset of streptococcal infection, and fever, elevated inflammatory markers and elevated streptococcal serology may be absent
claims.source_text: It may occur weeks to months after the onset of streptococcal infection depending on the history of disease recurrence and time of diagnosis, and thus fever, elevated concentrations of inflammatory markers and elevated streptococcal serology may be absent.

claims.claim: Hospitalisation for rheumatic fever is recommended to confirm the diagnosis and facilitate prompt access to an echocardiogram
claims.source_text: Hospitalisation for rheumatic fever is recommended to confirm the diagnosis and facilitate prompt access to an echocardiogram.

claims.claim: Initial analgesia is preferred during diagnostic uncertainty to avoid the masking effect that anti-inflammatory use can have on migratory joint symptoms, fever and inflammatory marker concentrations
claims.source_text: Initial analgesia is preferred during diagnostic uncertainty to avoid the masking effect that anti-inflammatory use can have on migratory joint symptoms, fever and concentrations of inflammatory markers.

claims.claim: Initial analgesia for mild to moderate pain is paracetamol 1000 mg (children 15 mg/kg) orally every four hours as needed up to a maximum of 60 mg/kg/day or 4000 mg/day
claims.source_text: Paracetamol 1000 mg (in children: 15 mg/kg) orally, every four hours as needed up to a maximum of 60 mg/kg/day or 4000 mg/day

claims.claim: Initial analgesia for severe pain is tramadol immediate-release 50-100 mg (children 1-2 mg/kg) orally every four hours as needed up to 400 mg/day, usually avoided in children under 12 due to variable metabolism
claims.source_text: Tramadol immediate-release 50-100 mg (in children: 1-2 mg/kg) orally, every four hours as needed up to a maximum of 400 mg/day ... Tramadol (or codeine) is usually avoided in children <12 years of age due to variable metabolism. Use only when strong analgesia is essential and cautious monitoring is available.

claims.claim: The 2020 guideline shortened secondary prophylaxis duration for some people without cardiac involvement, made NSAIDs such as naproxen or ibuprofen first-line for arthritis instead of aspirin, removed the contraindication of lidocaine with intramuscular benzathine benzylpenicillin G, and extended endocarditis prophylaxis to all patients with rheumatic heart disease rather than only Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people
claims.source_text: The duration of secondary prophylaxis after a diagnosis of acute rheumatic fever or rheumatic heart disease is now shorter for some people without cardiac involvement. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) such as naproxen or ibuprofen are now the recommended first-line drugs for arthritis instead of aspirin. Lidocaine (lignocaine) is no longer contraindicated with intramuscular injections of benzathine benzylpenicillin G. Endocarditis prophylaxis is now recommended for all patients with rheumatic heart disease, not just for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.

claims.claim: Eradication of the inciting streptococcal infection uses benzathine benzylpenicillin G 1,200,000 units (child under 20 kg 600,000 units, 20 kg or over 1,200,000 units) intramuscularly as a single dose
claims.source_text: Benzathine benzylpenicillin G 1,200,000 units (child <20 kg: 600,000 units, >=20 kg: 1,200,000 units) intramuscularly, single dose

claims.claim: Second-line eradication is phenoxymethylpenicillin 500 mg (child 15 mg/kg up to 500 mg) orally every 12 hours for 10 days
claims.source_text: Phenoxymethylpenicillin 500 mg (child: 15 mg/kg up to 500 mg) orally, every 12 hours for 10 days

claims.claim: For non-severe penicillin hypersensitivity, cefalexin 1 g (child 25 mg/kg up to 1 g) orally every 12 hours for 10 days, and for immediate penicillin hypersensitivity azithromycin 500 mg (child 12 mg/kg up to 500 mg) orally daily for 5 days
claims.source_text: For patients with penicillin hypersensitivity (non-severe): cefalexin 1 g (child: 25 mg/kg up to 1 g) orally, every 12 hours for 10 days ... For patients with immediate penicillin hypersensitivity: azithromycin 500 mg (child: 12 mg/kg up to 500 mg) orally, daily for 5 days

claims.claim: Streptococcal infection may not be evident by the time acute rheumatic fever manifests as cultures are often negative, but eradication therapy is still recommended, and intramuscular penicillin is preferred due to better adherence and its subsequent ongoing use in secondary prophylaxis
claims.source_text: Streptococcal infection may not be evident by the time acute rheumatic fever manifests (e.g. cultures often negative), but eradication therapy for possible persisting streptococci is recommended. Intramuscular penicillin is preferred as streptococcal eradication therapy due to better adherence and its subsequent ongoing use in secondary prophylaxis.

claims.claim: The inciting streptococcal infection can be treated with the first dose of benzathine benzylpenicillin G administered for ongoing secondary prophylaxis
claims.source_text: The inciting streptococcal infection can be treated with the first dose of benzathine benzylpenicillin G administered for ongoing secondary prophylaxis.

claims.claim: First-line arthritis treatment is naproxen immediate-release 250-500 mg (children 10-20 mg/kg/day) orally twice daily up to a maximum of 1250 mg daily
claims.source_text: Naproxen immediate-release 250-500 mg (in children: 10-20 mg/kg/day) orally twice daily, up to a maximum of 1250 mg daily

claims.claim: Second-line arthritis treatment is ibuprofen 200-400 mg (children 5-10 mg/kg) orally three times daily up to a maximum of 2400 mg daily, and third-line aspirin 50-60 mg/kg/day in 4-5 divided doses escalating to a maximum of 80-100 mg/kg/day
claims.source_text: Ibuprofen 200-400 mg (in children: 5-10 mg/kg) orally three times daily, up to a maximum of 2400 mg daily ... Aspirin 50-60 mg/kg/day orally, in 4-5 divided doses in adults and children. Dose can be escalated up to a maximum of 80-100 mg/kg/day in 4-5 divided doses

claims.claim: Naproxen may be safer than aspirin and convenient due to twice-daily dosing and the availability of oral suspension, while there are fewer data and less experience with ibuprofen for acute rheumatic fever
claims.source_text: Naproxen may be safer than aspirin and convenient due to twice-daily dosing and the availability of oral suspension. Ibuprofen is well tolerated and readily available, but there are less data and experience with its use for acute rheumatic fever than those associated with naproxen.

claims.claim: The dose of NSAIDs needed for acute rheumatic fever is generally higher than the dose recommended for other conditions so it may be appropriate to start at the higher dose range
claims.source_text: The dose of NSAIDs needed for acute rheumatic fever is generally higher than the dose recommended for other conditions; therefore, it may be appropriate to start at the higher dose range.

claims.claim: Due to the rare possibility of Reye's syndrome in children, aspirin may need to be discontinued during intercurrent acute viral illness, and influenza vaccination is strongly recommended
claims.source_text: Due to the rare possibility of Reye's syndrome in children, aspirin may need to be discontinued during intercurrent acute viral illness; thus, influenza vaccination is strongly recommended

claims.claim: Initial high-dose NSAID therapy weaned after 1-2 weeks is usual, most episodes resolve within six weeks and 90% within 12 weeks, and a rebound in inflammatory symptoms can occur on ceasing treatment requiring re-introduction
claims.source_text: Initial high-dose NSAID therapy, weaned after 1-2 weeks, is usual. ... Most episodes of acute rheumatic fever resolve within six weeks and 90% resolve within 12 weeks. A rebound in inflammatory symptoms can occur on ceasing treatment, requiring the drugs to be re-introduced.

claims.claim: There is no targeted drug therapy available for cardiac valve damage during the acute inflammatory stage
claims.source_text: There is no targeted drug therapy available for cardiac valve damage during the acute inflammatory stage.

claims.claim: Corticosteroids are recommended for severe carditis as prednisolone 1-2 mg/kg up to a maximum of 80 mg orally once daily, although meta-analyses suggest lack of benefit in preventing subsequent rheumatic heart disease and the studies mostly predate echocardiography, with expert opinion recommending corticosteroids for carditis associated with heart failure
claims.source_text: For severe carditis, corticosteroids are recommended ... Prednisolone 1-2 mg/kg up to a maximum of 80 mg orally once daily ... However, meta-analyses have suggested their lack of benefit in preventing subsequent rheumatic heart disease, although the studies were mostly performed before the availability of echocardiography. Expert opinion recommends corticosteroids for carditis associated with heart failure.

claims.claim: Screening for and management of latent infections such as hepatitis B, strongyloidiasis and tuberculosis are required before or on starting immunosuppressive corticosteroid doses
claims.source_text: Screening for and the management of latent infections (e.g. hepatitis B, strongyloidiasis, tuberculosis) are required before or on starting immunosuppressive corticosteroid doses.

claims.claim: Hydroxychloroquine has been used as a targeted disease-modifying agent based on promising in vitro findings but clinical trial data are not yet available
claims.source_text: Hydroxychloroquine has been used as a targeted disease-modifying agent based on promising in vitro findings, but clinical trial data are not yet available.

claims.claim: Pharmacotherapy is not needed for mild chorea, and treatment should be considered if movements interfere substantially with normal activities
claims.source_text: Pharmacotherapy is not needed for mild chorea. ... Treatment of Sydenham chorea should be considered if movements interfere substantially with normal activities.

claims.claim: Carbamazepine 3.5-10 mg/kg per dose orally twice daily is first line for moderate to severe chorea, followed by sodium valproate 7.5-10 mg/kg per dose orally twice daily
claims.source_text: Carbamazepine 3.5-10 mg/kg per dose orally twice daily ... Sodium valproate 7.5-10 mg/kg per dose orally twice daily

claims.claim: A chorea treatment response may not be observed for 1-2 weeks, drugs may only reduce rather than eliminate chorea, and treatment should continue for 2-4 weeks after chorea has subsided then be withdrawn
claims.source_text: A treatment response may not be observed for 1-2 weeks, and drugs may only reduce, not eliminate, chorea. Treatment should be continued for 2-4 weeks after chorea has subsided, and then be withdrawn.

claims.claim: Secondary antibiotic prophylaxis is the only treatment confirmed to be associated with a long-term reduction in the severity of rheumatic heart disease
claims.source_text: Secondary antibiotic prophylaxis is the only treatment confirmed to be associated with a long-term reduction in the severity of rheumatic heart disease.

claims.claim: Secondary prophylaxis is benzathine benzylpenicillin G by deep intramuscular injection 1,200,000 units for 20 kg and over or 600,000 units under 20 kg, every 28 days, or every 21 days for selected groups
claims.source_text: Benzathine benzylpenicillin G by deep intramuscular injection 1,200,000 units (>=20 kg) or 600,000 units (<20 kg) ... Every 28 days. Every 21 days for selected groups.

claims.claim: Oral alternatives for secondary prophylaxis are phenoxymethylpenicillin 250 mg orally twice daily, or erythromycin 250 mg orally twice daily for penicillin hypersensitivity, with intramuscular penicillin preferred due to greater effectiveness in head-to-head trial and better adherence
claims.source_text: Phenoxymethylpenicillin (penicillin V) 250 mg orally twice daily OR For patients with penicillin hypersensitivity (non-severe) or immediate penicillin hypersensitivity: erythromycin 250 mg orally twice daily ... Intramuscular penicillin is preferred due to greater effectiveness in head-to-head trial and better adherence.

claims.claim: Benzathine benzylpenicillin G every 21 days may be considered for patients with breakthrough acute rheumatic fever despite complete adherence to a 28-day regimen, and for patients at high risk of adverse consequences such as severe rheumatic heart disease or a history of heart valve surgery
claims.source_text: Benzathine benzylpenicillin G given every 21 days may be considered for: patients who have breakthrough acute rheumatic fever despite complete adherence to a 28-day regimen; patients who are at a high risk of adverse consequences if acute rheumatic fever occurs (have severe rheumatic heart disease or a history of heart valve surgery).

claims.claim: Patients on 28-day regimens can be recalled from 21 days to help ensure that injections are given by day 28
claims.source_text: Patients on 28-day regimens can be recalled from 21 days to help ensure that injections are given by day 28.

claims.claim: Increasing adherence to benzathine benzylpenicillin G is associated with improved rheumatic fever outcomes, and regular oral penicillin is not as effective potentially due to serum penicillin concentrations achieved and problems with adherence
claims.source_text: Increasing adherence to benzathine benzylpenicillin G is associated with improved rheumatic fever outcomes. Regular oral penicillin is not as effective than benzathine benzylpenicillin G. This is potentially due to the serum penicillin concentrations achieved and problems with adherence.

claims.claim: For children weighing less than 10 kg a dose of 600,000 units is still generally recommended but paediatric advice should be sought for careful planning of the secondary prophylaxis regimen
claims.source_text: For children weighing less than 10 kg, a dose of 600,000 units is still generally recommended, but seek paediatric advice for careful planning of the secondary prophylaxis regimen.

claims.claim: Possible acute rheumatic fever without cardiac involvement requires 12 months of prophylaxis then reassessment
claims.source_text: Possible acute rheumatic fever (without cardiac involvement) | Incomplete features of acute rheumatic fever with a normal echocardiogram and normal ECG throughout acute rheumatic fever episodes | 12 months (then reassess)

claims.claim: Probable or definite acute rheumatic fever without cardiac involvement requires a minimum of 5 years after the most recent episode or until 21 years of age, whichever is longer
claims.source_text: Minimum of 5 years after the most recent episode of acute rheumatic fever, or until 21 years of age (whichever is longer)

claims.claim: Borderline rheumatic heart disease in people 20 years or under in a high-risk setting requires a minimum of 2 years following diagnosis, continuing another 2 years and reassessing with specialist input if still present
claims.source_text: In a high-risk setting: minimum of 2 years following the diagnosis of borderline rheumatic heart disease. If borderline rheumatic heart disease is still present at 2 years, continue for another 2 years and reassess. Seek specialist input

claims.claim: Mild rheumatic heart disease with documented acute rheumatic fever requires a minimum of 10 years after the most recent episode or until 21 years of age, whichever is longer
claims.source_text: Mild rheumatic heart disease | ... If there is a documented history of acute rheumatic fever: minimum of 10 years after the most recent episode of acute rheumatic fever, or until 21 years of age (whichever is longer)

claims.claim: Moderate rheumatic heart disease with documented acute rheumatic fever requires a minimum of 10 years after the most recent episode or until 35 years of age, whichever is longer
claims.source_text: Moderate rheumatic heart disease | Moderate rheumatic heart disease on echocardiography | If there is a documented history of acute rheumatic fever: minimum of 10 years after the most recent episode of acute rheumatic fever or until 35 years of age (whichever is longer)

claims.claim: Severe rheumatic heart disease, or previous valve repair or prosthetic valve replacement, with documented acute rheumatic fever requires a minimum of 10 years after the most recent episode or until 40 years of age, whichever is longer
claims.source_text: Severe rheumatic heart disease | Severe rheumatic heart disease on echocardiography OR Previous valve repair or prosthetic valve replacement | If there is a documented history of acute rheumatic fever: minimum of 10 years after the most recent episode of acute rheumatic fever or until 40 years of age (whichever is longer)

claims.claim: If diagnosed with mild or moderate rheumatic heart disease and aged 35 or over without acute rheumatic fever, secondary prophylaxis is not required, and if diagnosed with severe rheumatic heart disease at 40 or over without acute rheumatic fever specialist input is required
claims.source_text: If diagnosed with mild or moderate rheumatic heart disease and aged >=35 years (without acute rheumatic fever), secondary prophylaxis is not required. ... If a person is diagnosed with severe rheumatic heart disease at >=40 years of age (without acute rheumatic fever), specialist input is required to determine the need for secondary prophylaxis.

claims.claim: The risk of acute rheumatic fever recurrence is low in people 40 years and over, however lifelong secondary prophylaxis is usually recommended for patients who have had or are likely to need heart valve surgery
claims.source_text: The risk of acute rheumatic fever recurrence is low in people >=40 years of age; however, lifelong secondary prophylaxis is usually recommended for patients who have had, or are likely to need, heart valve surgery.

claims.claim: Prophylaxis may be considered for longer in women considering pregnancy who live in high-risk circumstances for acute rheumatic fever
claims.source_text: Prophylaxis may be considered for longer in women considering pregnancy who live in high-risk circumstances for acute rheumatic fever.

claims.claim: All people receiving secondary prophylaxis require a comprehensive clinical assessment and echocardiogram before cessation, and risk factors including future exposure to environments with a high burden of group A streptococcus must be considered
claims.source_text: All people receiving secondary prophylaxis require a comprehensive clinical assessment and echocardiogram before cessation. Risk factors including future exposure to environments with a high burden of group A streptococcus must be considered.

claims.claim: An update in March 2022 recommends secondary prophylaxis for people 20 years or under living in high-risk settings without a documented history of acute rheumatic fever but with an echocardiogram showing borderline rheumatic heart disease
claims.source_text: An update in March 2022 recommends secondary prophylaxis for people <=20 years of age living in high-risk settings without a documented history of acute rheumatic fever but who have an echocardiogram showing borderline rheumatic heart disease.

claims.claim: Moderate or severe rheumatic heart disease may rarely improve on echocardiography without valve surgery, in which case the conditions for ceasing prophylaxis follow the most recent severity category
claims.source_text: Rarely, moderate or severe rheumatic heart disease may improve on echocardiography without valve surgery. In these cases, the conditions for ceasing prophylaxis can change to follow the most recent severity category.

claims.claim: S. pyogenes remains susceptible to penicillin as it is unable to genetically express resistance to penicillin
claims.source_text: S. pyogenes remains susceptible to penicillin, as it is unable to genetically express resistance to penicillin.

claims.claim: An estimated 3.2% of people have an allergic reaction to penicillin and 0.2% have anaphylactic reactions
claims.source_text: An estimated 3.2% of people have an allergic reaction to penicillin and 0.2% have anaphylactic reactions.

claims.claim: Macrolides cover approximately 88% of S. pyogenes isolates in Northern Territory Top End antibiogram data due to class resistance to macrolides and clindamycin in some isolates, the regional proportion is related to local prescribing practices, and macrolides remain an acceptable second-line option as long as most isolates remain susceptible
claims.source_text: They cover approximately 88% of S. pyogenes isolates (Northern Territory Top End antibiogram data) due to the development of class resistance to macrolides and clindamycin in some isolates. The proportion of S. pyogenes resistant to macrolides in any region is related to local prescribing practices. As long as most S. pyogenes isolates remain susceptible, macrolides are an acceptable second-line option.

claims.claim: Between 3% and 30% of group A streptococcus isolates internationally are resistant to macrolide antibiotics
claims.source_text: Between 3% and 30% of group A streptococcus isolates internationally are resistant to macrolide antibiotics (e.g., azithromycin).

claims.claim: For non-severe penicillin hypersensitivity use cefalexin to treat the inciting streptococcal infection and erythromycin for secondary prophylaxis, and for immediate penicillin hypersensitivity use azithromycin for the inciting infection and erythromycin for secondary prophylaxis
claims.source_text: For non-severe penicillin hypersensitivity, use cefalexin to treat the inciting streptococcal infection and erythromycin for secondary prophylaxis. For immediate penicillin hypersensitivity, use azithromycin to treat the inciting streptococcal infection and erythromycin for secondary prophylaxis

claims.claim: The weight of evidence now favours antibiotic use for infective endocarditis prophylaxis in all patients with rheumatic heart disease undergoing high-risk dental or other surgical procedures
claims.source_text: The weight of evidence now favours antibiotic use for infective endocarditis prophylaxis in all patients with rheumatic heart disease undergoing high-risk dental or other surgical procedures.

claims.claim: Endocarditis prophylaxis is amoxicillin 2 g (children 50 mg/kg up to 2 g) 60 minutes before the procedure
claims.source_text: For endocarditis prophylaxis | Amoxicillin 2 g (in children: 50 mg/kg up to 2 g) | 60 minutes

claims.claim: For delayed non-severe penicillin hypersensitivity cefalexin 2 g (children 50 mg/kg up to 2 g) 60 minutes before, and for immediate or delayed severe hypersensitivity clindamycin 600 mg (children 20 mg/kg up to 600 mg) 60-120 minutes before
claims.source_text: For patients with delayed non-severe hypersensitivity to penicillins, cefalexin can be used in most cases | Cefalexin 2 g (in children: 50 mg/kg up to 2 g) | 60 minutes ... Clindamycin 600 mg (in children: 20 mg/kg up to 600 mg) | 60-120 minutes

claims.claim: Amoxicillin is first-line for endocarditis prophylaxis even in patients receiving benzathine benzylpenicillin G for secondary prophylaxis
claims.source_text: Amoxicillin is the recommended first-line drug for endocarditis prophylaxis for certain dental procedures in patients with specified cardiac conditions including rheumatic heart disease, even in those receiving benzathine benzylpenicillin G for secondary prophylaxis

claims.claim: If a patient has recently had a treatment course of penicillin, amoxicillin or another beta-lactam, clindamycin is the recommended first-line drug because the treatment course may have reduced the amoxicillin susceptibility of viridans streptococci
claims.source_text: However, if a patient has recently had a course of treatment with penicillin, amoxicillin or another beta-lactam (providing higher antibiotic concentrations than prophylactic doses), clindamycin is the recommended first-line drug. This is because the treatment course may have reduced the amoxicillin susceptibility of viridans streptococci

claims.claim: There is some evidence that moxifloxacin may be used as an alternative to clindamycin in patients with immediate or delayed hypersensitivity to penicillins but this has not been validated
claims.source_text: There is some evidence to suggest that moxifloxacin may be used as an alternative to clindamycin in patients with immediate (severe) or non-severe or delayed hypersensitivity to penicillins, but this has not been validated.

claims.claim: Groups at high risk include people living in an acute rheumatic fever endemic setting, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people living in rural or remote areas, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and Maori and Pacific Islander people living in metropolitan households affected by crowding or low socioeconomic status, and patients with a personal history of acute rheumatic fever or rheumatic heart disease under 40 years of age
claims.source_text: People living in an acute rheumatic fever-endemic setting; Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people living in rural or remote areas; Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and Maori and Pacific Islander people living in metropolitan households affected by crowding or low socioeconomic status; Patients with a personal history of acute rheumatic fever or rheumatic heart disease and <40 years of age

claims.claim: Those who may be at high risk include people with a family or household recent history of acute rheumatic fever or rheumatic heart disease, household overcrowding of more than 2 people per bedroom or low socioeconomic status, and migrants or refugees from low- or middle-income countries and their children
claims.source_text: Family or household recent history of acute rheumatic fever or rheumatic heart disease; People with household overcrowding (>2 people/bedroom) or low socioeconomic status; Migrants or refugees from low- or middle-income countries and their children

claims.claim: An acute rheumatic fever endemic setting refers to communities with acute rheumatic fever incidence higher than 30 per 100,000 per year in those aged 5-14 years and rheumatic heart disease all-age prevalence higher than 2 per 1000
claims.source_text: This refers to communities where the rates of acute rheumatic fever and rheumatic heart disease are high (for example, an acute rheumatic fever incidence higher than 30/100,000 per year in those aged 5-14 years and a rheumatic heart disease all-age prevalence higher than 2/1000).

claims.claim: Patients with moderate to severe rheumatic heart disease require cardiology services and regular echocardiographic follow-up, and women with rheumatic heart disease who are pregnant or of childbearing age require pre-conception counselling and specialist care
claims.source_text: Patients with moderate to severe rheumatic heart disease require cardiology services and regular echocardiographic follow-up. Women with rheumatic heart disease who are pregnant or of childbearing age require pre-conception counselling and specialist care.

claims.claim: Echocardiography after cessation of prophylaxis is at 1, 3 and 5 years for probable and definite acute rheumatic fever and mild rheumatic heart disease, initially every 12 months for moderate, and initially every 6 months for severe
claims.source_text: At 1, 3 and 5 years ... Moderate rheumatic heart disease ... Initially every 12 months ... Severe rheumatic heart disease ... Initially every 6 months

claims.claim: In less than 10% of the population infection with Streptococcus pyogenes can trigger autoimmune conditions including acute rheumatic fever or acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis days to months after the initial infection
claims.source_text: In less than 10% of the population, infection with Streptococcus pyogenes (group A streptococcus) can trigger autoimmune conditions including acute rheumatic fever or acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis days to months after the initial infection.
